A central London authority could double its council tax to prevent cuts to services following a government decision to redirect funding towards more deprived areas.

Westminster City Council has warned it faces "stark and very tough choices" as a result of changes made under the "fair funding" review of council allocations.

This review is set to halve its annual central grant, plummeting from £219 million to £119 million by the 2029-30 financial year.

The Conservative-run council, which collects more than £2.5 billion in business rates, argues the Government’s calculations overlooked high rates of poverty and social challenges within the borough.

It also contends the review failed to account for the significant pressures placed on services by its one million daily visitors.

Westminster, along with five other councils, has been granted two-year "funding realignment powers", enabling it to increase council tax beyond the standard 5% threshold.

This effectively signals that the Government expects the authority to hike council tax significantly to make up for lost funding, Westminster said.

The council, which has one of the lowest average council tax levels in the country, will consult residents this summer on what services they value most and their willingness to pay higher bills.

Cabinet member Paul Fisher said: “The Government assumes we are now going to put up council tax by 75–100% to make up our immediate budget shortfall.

The council, which has one of the lowest average council tax levels in the country, will consult residents this summer on what services they value most and their willingness to pay higher bills ( PA Wire )

“Whilst we have not yet settled on council tax levels for next year, this new financial climate is unprecedented and presents us with stark and very tough choices ahead where there are no easy options.”

He added that “extensive efficiencies and transformation plans” would not cover the budget shortfall in the coming years, so residents will be asked if they are prepared to pay more council tax.

Mr Fisher added: “Whilst we will continue to fight for Westminster residents and take our case to the Government, we need to be honest that there is no easy option here and no horizon in which we do not have to make savings.

“We charge the second lowest council tax in the country, provide cost efficient services and collect more than £2.5 billion in business rates – yet we are effectively being forced into making huge savings, with likely cuts and expected council tax increases.

“Even if we doubled our council tax, we would still be one of the lowest in London and the country.”

A Labour source said: “The fair funding formula is about directing money to the areas in Britain’s most deprived communities around the entire country.

“I don’t think even Westminster council would think that they are top of that particular list.”

The Local Government Association said that despite the funding reforms, councils in England are facing a £7 billion funding black hole within three years, a gap which is more than the current council spend on roads, transport, homelessness and housing services combined.

Band D properties in Westminster are currently charged £1,047 a year in council tax.

The four other councils granted funding realignment powers are City of London, Hammersmith and Fulham, Kensington and Chelsea, Wandsworth and Windsor & Maidenhead.

A total of seven other councils have been permitted to increase council tax to a specific level.

News.content:
Aryna Sabalenka admits to never having tried Wimbledon’s strawberries and cream, but has pledged to change that as she looks to win her first title on grass.

Against Jelena Ostapenko in the third round, Sabalenka eased to a 6-4, 6-4 victory in little more than an hour-and-a-half to set up an enticing clash with high-flying Naomi Osaka.

News.title: Silverstone in ecstasy as Lewis Hamilton grabs British GP sprint pole
News.content:
If this year’s British Grand Prix weekend carries on like this, we could be in for something truly special.

Lewis Hamilton sent Silverstone’s packed grandstands into raptures on Friday by claiming a stunning pole for Saturday’s sprint race.

Race organisers are expecting an all-time Formula One record crowd of 565,000 fans over the course of the weekend, with about 150,000 turning up on Friday. They could not have asked for a better storyline.

Hamilton, who thrust himself into title contention with his maiden victory for Ferrari in Spain last month, is hoping for what would be a record-breaking 10th win at his home race. And the 41-year-old seven-time world champion had the perfect opening day, topping practice and then edging Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli by 0.011sec in sprint qualifying.

News.title: Relentless Djokovic stays in the hunt for unprecedented 25th grand slam
News.content:
Hello and welcome to coverage from Wimbledon as Novak Djokovic takes on Arthur Rinderknech.

The seven-time champion was in imperious form on Wednesday as he eased past Stefanos Tsitsipas in straight-sets under the roof.

Today he opens the schedule on Centre Court against Frenchman Rinderknech.

“Obviously you feel very happy, satisfied and joyful on the court when you are playing this way,” Djokovic said after beating Tsitsipas.

“I’m feeling great. I try not to take these moments for granted when ​playing on the Centre Court of Wimbledon. I feel ‌very privileged to be walking out on this court at age 30-plus. I don’t think it’s a cliche because I actually believe it’s true, but age is just a number.”

The Serbian is expected to step out again sporting a ‌cream ​blazer and if he wins today, he will be one victory shy of ​matching Roger Federer’s men’s record of 105 match-wins at Wimbledon.

Djokovic suffered a couple of slips on Wednesday but he is not overly concerned.

“It’s grass,” he said. “You’re going to fall more than any other surface. That’s one. And two, you’re going to probably have even more risk of falling if the roof is closed because the grass is slippery. There’s more moist, there’s more humidity. It’s more slippery on the court.

“With my kind of movement that is quite dynamic, yeah, I mean, I’ve been lucky so far that nothing really major in a bad way has happened. It’s not something you can predict. It’s not something that you can - how can I say - prevent, as well. In the heat of the moment, you’re fighting, battling, it can happen.”

News.title: I’ve camped on every continent. This is the best gear (and what you can do without)
News.content:
I didn’t grow up camping. In fact, I didn’t stay on a campsite until I was an adult. Since discovering the joys of sleeping outside while on assignment in Australia, I have been a complete convert.

I’ve camped on every continent, in all four seasons and in all weathers. I’ve slept in hammocks, bivvies, tents and portaledges. In 2018 I undertook a 10-night Extreme Sleep Out for charity, suspending myself off 10 UK landmarks. I’ve slept on top of the British Three Peaks (the highest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales), bivvied at the extreme points of mainland Britain and walked its entire length camping for 40 nights in a row.

And not quite as extreme but definitely just as challenging, I’ve taken my young son camping since he was two, and even persuaded my 77-year-old dad to kayak to an island in the Thames and hammock camp with me.

Overseas, I’ve slept out on ledges in Wadi Rum with the Bedouin, wild camped in Saudi Arabia, completed a solo crossing in Greenland from ice cap to ocean with my trusty tent, bivouacked on the Great Barrier Reef, cliff camped in Colorado and even slept out with no tent in Antarctica.

All these adventures have taught me the importance of good kit – and the perils of bad gear.

News.title: Five reasons why Spain may present biggest threat to France
News.content:
Dancing Yamal

It was a game when Lamine Yamal was probably overshadowed by the menace on the other wing, Álex Baena, but the Barcelona prodigy still produced some gorgeous moments, including four nutmegs, three of which were inflicted on poor Konrad Laimer. It was telling that the Austria coach Ralf Rangnick had shifted Laimer to left back, like he had done against Argentina, in a bid to stymie Yamal but even then Marcel Sabitzer was tasked with doubling up at times. Laimer was glad he did in the first half when nutmegged and left for dead by Yamal.

Only two fine stops from Schalager denied him a goal. Groin and hamstring problems have curtailed the 18-year-old’s involvement but there were clear signs of him stepping it up a couple of gears here and, in a tournament in which the superstar players have really stood up, De la Fuente will be delighted if Yamal can deliver his best at the business end. “Little by little I’m starting to feel like myself,” he said after this. “Making the runs I need, the dribbles, everything.” Not words opponents will want to hear.

Cucurella-Baena combination

Austria could not deal with Spain’s threat down the left. Baena looks quite the stand-in for the injury-dogged Nico Williams. The Atlético Madrid forward worked to devastating effect down the left in tandem with the outstanding Marc Cucurella – who set up the first and third goals and had a hand in the second – to routinely overload Austria.

The first goal was a case in point. With Baena cleverly positioned inside, he sucked in the Austria right-back Stefan Posch to create the space for Pedri to find Cucurella on the outside. His cross was then coolly finished by Oyarzabal. With Porro and Yamal on the opposite side, Spain are a huge threat on both flanks.

Underestimate Oyarzabal at your peril

The Real Sociedad forward may not be quite the household name of some of the strikers at this tournament, but he is integral to Spain’s success and way of playing – added to that he has taken his fine club form into this World Cup. Two expertly taken finishes pointed to his threat in front of goal, but it is his clever movement and positioning, not to mention his work rate, that makes him such a nuisance in attack.

News.title: England dispatch South Africa to set up final showdown with Australia
News.content:
England put their trials and tribulations of the past few years behind them to reach a first major final for four years, beating South Africa by 40 runs to book a meeting with Australia at Lord’s on Sunday.

The first innings was a return to the old ways when England lost three quick wickets and then had to turn to the experience of Nat Sciver-Brunt and Heather Knight to salvage their hopes from 23 for three to finish with 169.

In the past two years, England might have changed the coach, the captain, a handful of backroom staff and the playing style, but it still came down to the two most experienced batters to dig them out of a difficult situation.

Knight and Sciver-Brunt put on 133 runs for the fourth wicket, playing with calm and composure at the crease and scoring boundaries at regular enough intervals to put the pressure on South Africa, and, in doing so, ensure they would be in Sunday’s final.

“I was very nervous going in, and I suppose quite emotional about it yesterday,” Sciver-Brunt said.

“Just the occasion and what we’ve been able to do as a team, so trying to live up to the three games that I missed and have an impact as a leader and as a batter.

“I managed to put those thoughts to bed for the warm-up starting and I suppose this is the moment where we switch onto game mode. So I’m just so excited and proud of what I’ve been able to do today.”

Sports.title: ‘It’s ruining me’ – England fan ‘beyond frustrated’ and £1,300 out of pocket after Mexico World Cup kick-off changed
Sports.content:
ENGLAND fans have been forced to scramble and reschedule their flights after reports emerged that their World Cup last-16 showdown against Mexico is being MOVED to 12pm local time, amid severe storm warnings.

And the brutal disruption to their travel plans is costing Three Lions supporters an absolute fortune.





Many fans had planned to land in Mexico City on Sunday morning for the original 6pm local kick-off, with some connecting from Atlanta and others travelling up from Cancun.

One gutted England fan, Gavin Walsh, spoke exclusively to SunSport about his logistical nightmare after being forced to shell out over £1,000 just to alter his itinerary.

He said: “It’s ruining me. It’s ruined me being able to spend the 4th of July in the States with my family.

“I’m beyond confused and frustrated. How on earth has it been changed two and a half days before kick-off?



“I’m still in Atlanta now. I have to fly to Orlando now to get to Mexico City, as opposed to a direct flight, it would have been perfect.

“I was supposed to land in Mexico City at 9:55 am on Sunday, so I’d have plenty of time to get to the game at 6pm.

“It’s proper squeaky bum time, I feel like my whole career of travelling prepared me for this moment.

“I’ve had to book another flight for tomorrow, which has cost me an extra £1,300. My original flight was £2,800, so it’s cost a total of £4,100.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“Delta offers credits, I think, but I don’t think I’ll get my money back.

“It’s not even about me. What about the fans who haven’t had the chance to cover additional travel costs, or who get notified too late?

“It has left them no time to make arrangements or plans.”

Terrifying weather forecasts around the Estadio Azteca have panicked tournament organisers into bringing the massive knockout clash forward to midday local time on Sunday.

The dramatic story first emerged to SunSport from a source working inside the Azteca.



Fifa is currently locked in ongoing talks, and SunSport understands that the FA were officially informed on Friday that moving the game forward is now a distinct possibility.

Gavin is just one of thousands of furious fans facing immense frustration at Fifa and tournament chiefs, who have failed to communicate the chaos earlier than now.

Severe storms threaten the original later slot, while the new 12 pm kick-off promises much safer conditions with a forecasted 21°C and cloudy skies.

Sports.title: Australia coach’s 119th-minute tactical switch horribly backfires after World Cup penalty shootout defeat to Egypt
Sports.content:
AUSTRALIA’S extra-time gamble of subbing on a penalty specialist failed to pay off in their World Cup exit to Egypt.

Socceroos coach Paul Okon brought on goalkeeper Matt Ryan in the 119th minute in order to stop the spotkicks.





Ryan is known as something of a penalty specialist and had saved 11 of the 30 penalties he faced in his career before this shootout.

But the decision was still met by some confusion and amazement on commentary.

Lead commentaor Robyn Cowen said: “What have we got here?”

The co-commentator also called it the “most penalty shootout sub you’ll ever see.”



Working for Australia was the fact that Egypt had lost their previous FOUR shootouts.

But things didn’t go to plan for the Socceroos.

Harry Souttar, who was instrumental in helping Australia equalise in open play, went first and blazed his effort over the crossbar to put the pressure on Ryan’s shoulders.

The Levante keeper clearly failed to strike fear into Mohamed Salah as the now former Liverpool star dinked a paneka down the middle.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

He said after the game: “I don’t know if this will be my last World Cup or not, so I had to do it!”

Ryan ended up failing to save any of Egypt’s penalties as they went 100 percent from their four spot kicks and Australia had to pack their bags.

The game was 1-1 after 90 minutes in a really physical affair.

Egypt took an early lead against the Socceroos through Emam Ashour as the Aussies struggled to get a grip on the tie.



However, a more scrappy second half suited Okon’s men and a Mohamed Hany own goal from an Australia set-piece put them back on level terms.

Still, extra-time always looked like it was heading for penalties and Okon clearly had a plan for that eventuality.

Unfortunately for the Aussies, it did not work.

Sports.title: Australia 1 Egypt 1 (2-4 on pens): Pharaohs win first-ever World Cup knockout game to reach last-16
Sports.content:
MO Salah and Egypt buried the penalty curse of the Pharoahs to make their own history.

Under Salah’s captaincy, the team had twice tasted spotkick agony on the big occasion against Senegal – once in an AFCON final and then in a World Cup play-off.





The former Liverpool winger himself had missed in the latter shootout.

This time Salah, with the third penalty, and his side held their nerve to win their first knockout game at the finals.



Australia brought on former Brighton goalkeeper Mat Ryan towards the end of extra time specifically for the shootout.

But Aussie captain Harry Souttar and Lucas Herrington missed the Aussies’ first and fourth spotkicks.

And Egypt centre back Hossam Abdelmaguid completed a perfect set of penalties and made history for his country.

Salah, the Egyptian King, was far from his regal best for most of the match after rushing back from a hamstring injury suffered in the final group game against Iran.



Yet when it came to the crunch, he did what he had to do to help his team over the line.

Even with the skipper allegedly fit, boss Hossam Hassan still made five changes and was able to name only 12 substitutes, three of them goalkeepers.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Egypt’s left side had a completely new look because of injury and suspension, with Marmoush restored to the team to play wide.



Australia, in contrast, were unchanged from the goalless draw against Paraguay that sealed a place in the knockouts.

Tony Popovic’s settled side made the better start.

Forward Cristian Volpato hit the crossbar, then right wing back Jordan Bos charged through, only to be denied by a good challenge by Ramy Rabia.

But it was Egypt who took the lead in the 13th minute.

A free kick was only half cleared and left back Karim Hafez curled in a delicious cross which Ashour met with a firm, well-directed header.



There was little more goalmouth action for the rest of the half.

Australia had opportunities to cause trouble from set-pieces and long throws, with one leading to Aziz Behich hitting a shot from distance which Mostafa Shobeir saved comfortably.

Meanwhile Egypt seemed mostly content to sit on their lead and a stoppage-time challenge by Rabia on Bos was typical of their robust approach,

Bos did not come out for the second half but Egypt certainly did.

Marmoush was played through inside 10 seconds, only to send a right-footed shot wide with the goal at his mercy.



Australia made the most of their escape.

Despite some neat passing, a dead-ball situation remained their best bet.

Sure enough, New York City midfielder Aiden O’Neill provided the inswinging delivery and Hany could only head it into his own net.



The right back appeared to have been knocked unconscious moments earlier yet returned to the field to become only the second player to score two own goals at the same finals.

When Hassan prepared two substitutes for the last 25 minutes, you wondered if Salah would be one of the men replaced.

He was not and the faith was almost justified in stoppage time of normal time.

Neither side had created a clear-cut chance until Salah’s fabulous cross was met by Rabia’s head.



But Aussie goalkeeper Patrick Beach made a match-saving stop.

Then Salah teed up Haissem Hassan, only for his shot to be blocked by Leicester’s Harry Souttar.

Early in extra time, Salah sent a good chance over the bar with his less-than-trusty right foot.

The rest of the first half was uneventful.

Egypt were much the better team in the second, with Salah going on one trademark mazy run.



Popovic put on Ryan for Beach with a minute of extra time to go.

But Souttar missed with the Aussies’ first kick.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The next four penalties were all converted and up stepped Salah to clip it down the middle.

Then Herrington hit the bar and Abdelmaguid sent Egypt through to the last 16.

Sports.title: Fifa in talks to move SECOND match after looking to bring forward England kick-off with World Cup in chaos
Sports.content:
FIFA is scrambling to reshuffle TWO major knockout games, with the last-16 tie between Brazil and Norway at risk of moving.

World Cup chiefs are locked in talks to bring forward the kick-off time of England’s World Cup last-16 showdown against Mexico at the Azteca.





Both games are at risk of changing due to the risk of weather disruption in Mexico City, including flooding and thunderstorms.

A huge storm warning is threatening to devastate the Mexican capital in the late afternoon and early evening.

England‘s match against Mexico could be moved six hours earlier from 1am BST on Monday to 7pm BST on Sunday.

But the consequences could have a knock-on effect for the other game scheduled for Sunday.

And now discussions are also being held about pushing Brazil‘s clash against Norway.

Brazil and Norway are due to play at the MetLife Stadium outside new York at 4pm local time and 9pm BST.

A spokesperson for the Brazilian Football Federation said: “A change is possible and we are waiting on FIFA.”

Pulling England forward will trigger a total scheduling nightmare, throwing England onto a direct collision course with Brazil v Norway.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The English FA only found out about the potential rescheduling from journalists at a training session.

Extreme weather has already impacted one match in Mexico City during this World Cup.

Kick off in Mexico’s round-of-32 tie against Ecuador was pushed back by an hour due to thunder and lightning in the surrounding area.

France’s group-stage fixture against Iraq was delayed for over two hours because of safety concerns amid adverse weather conditions in Philadelphia.



The original kick-off time for the England match had prompted the UK government to allow pubs, which would usually close around 11pm BST, to stay open until 5am in order to show the match.

Meanwhile, England’s team hotel in Mexico is expected to have roadblocks around its perimeter to guard against pre-game disruption.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker hails Harry Kane as greatest English footballer EVER before making shock admission about World Cup hero
Sports.content:
GARY Lineker weighed up the question for a moment.

As one of our greatest-ever strikers, who scored 48 goals in 80 appearances for his country, where did he rank captain Harry Kane in English football folklore?





After a brief consideration of others in the frame, he came up with an answer as decisive as any of his trademark finishes during his football heyday.

He said: “Harry Kane is the best footballer we’ve ever produced.

“Not just the best striker, the best footballer.”

We were speaking in New York the day after Kane had bagged a double to dig England out of a hole against DR Congo in their last-32 World Cup knockout tie.



Lineker grew up listening to tales of the World Cup win in 1966, of Geoff Hurst’s hat-trick, of Bobby Moore’s captaincy, and Bobby Charlton’s genius.

And he played with the mercurial talent that was Paul Gascoigne.

But Kane, who has broken Lineker’s World Cup goals record, wins the argument hands down.

Lineker says: “I know people talk about Charlton and Moore and maybe a few others but I didn’t really see much of them, I was a little kid.



“You can only really judge players that you’ve seen regularly in your lifetime, and also Harry’s record speaks for itself.

“I know it’s seen by some as being easier now, when all records are being broken, because we’re playing extra games, and there are a lot more smaller nations.

“But, it’s the quality of his all-round game we’re talking about, not necessarily just the numbers, which are incredible.

“The way he drops into space and then holds the ball, the weight of passing, and his vision are all incredible. His finishing from one-on-ones, to outside the box, to in the air. He’s got it all, Harry.

“The only thing that’s missing is probably a yard of pace. I mean, if he had that, you’d be talking Kylian Mbappe great.



“He’s got a better all-round game than me. My own game was fine, and I could hold it up, and give it and go, but I didn’t have that passing range and wouldn’t score goals from outside the box.

“I knew I was good but Harry’s just on another level. I had a good knowledge of how to score goals and if you added that and my pace to his all-round game. I think that would be a very good player indeed!”

Lineker, of course, went on from playing to be a hugely successful TV presenter, hosting the BBC’s Match of the Day for more than a quarter of a century as well as countless World Cups.



And here comes the most astonishing revelation from our interview. I ask whether he’s ever sat down with Kane and compared their games. He replied: “I’ve never talked to him about it. In fact I’ve never even met him!”

He had to be joking. Lineker said: “No, I’ve interviewed him down the line for TV but never met him.

“It’s mad, isn’t it? I was saying it to people the other day and they’re going, ‘What?’ And I replied, ‘No, never’. I’m not sure anybody believes me but there it is.”

Having left the BBC, Lineker is approaching this World Cup from a different angle, hosting his The Rest is Football show for Netflix every day from New York.

He said: “Our studio is on the second floor in Times Square and it’s like mental there. There’s a real buzz with thousands of fans from all over the world and everyone’s getting on lovely, which is one of the great successes so far.



“Everything’s joyous. The world could learn a bit from that.

“I’m not going around all the venues to see how it’s taken off but the stadiums are all full.

“It’s overpriced, though. I don’t think we should be making plans to get a second mortgage to get a ticket when Fifa is supposedly a non-profit organisation. It’s bizarre to me. But football-wise, it’s been really good and we’ve had lots of great goals.

“We’ve got these three girls, who do our make-up, hair and wardrobe, and at the start of the tournament they didn’t know anything about the World Cup.

“Now they’re really into it. Maybe that’s my only way to judge it.



“It’s massive staging it over three countries but it’s gone well so far, better than I thought it would.

“The big stars have turned up and they’re all banging in the goals. The race for the Golden Boot is as interesting to me as the winner is. Lionel Messi is probably still the best in the world, to be perfectly honest. Nobody does what Messi does, he’s remarkable for his age. He’s not as quick as he was, you can see that, but he can still control a football match.

“He’s just not human. He’s not. He’s some kind of alien.”



England now face Mexico for their last-16 showdown in the Azteca Stadium, scene of Diego Maradona’s Hand of God goal 40 years ago.

What does Gary, who scored in that game, think about England’s chance of bringing it home?

He replied: “I still don’t think they’ve found their fluid game yet, they’re still working it out. I’m trying to watch them as though I’m neutral, even though I’m not, and for 20 minutes against DR Congo we were really poor.

“It was basically the shock of conceding an early goal, but then we got hold of them at the end of the first quarter.”

The first quarter Gary?!



He said: “I can’t believe I’m even saying that. Don’t get me started on the hydration breaks!

“If I was watching that game, and it was Brazil or Spain against Congo, I’d be thinking that it was cool and they played really well.

“I kept saying that we’d score.



“We’ve got two genuine superstars, in Kane and Jude Bellingham, and Declan Rice isn’t far off that as well. There’s a nucleus in there but, defensively, obviously slight concerns because we haven’t got much depth.

“The manager Thomas Tuchel has worked in England for a few years and he obviously knows his English football, and he’s bought into the team psyche. Personally, I think we should be able to find a coach of our own but, at the same time, if we win the World Cup, I don’t think it really matters a hoot. We can win it but it’s unlikely, especially with how good France look with that front four. World Cups are incredibly hard to win but we’re not without a chance.

“We can get a bit of momentum now from that comeback because there’s a bit more belief. That was a big deal.

“But the next one in Mexico, with all the challenges that brings, is really tough.”

Sports.title: England fans ‘being treated like dirt’ after ‘outrageous’ decision to move Mexico World Cup clash leaving some stranded
Sports.content:
ENGLAND fans have hit out at the decision to move the last-16 clash against Mexico.

The Three Lions were expected to face Mexico at the Estadio Azteca on Monday at 1am UK time.





Fifa chiefs are currently in talks to bring the kick-off forward by six hours due to weather concerns.

This means the match will now start at 12pm local time and 7pm UK time.

The change will be a relief to fans at home who no longer face a long night watching the drama unfold.

However, supporters who have travelled across the Atlantic Ocean have had a major change to their plans.



Some fans had planned to fly into Mexico City on Sunday ahead of kick-off.

They could now face missing the game due to the earlier start time unless they are able to swap flight times.

As the news has broken, fans have taken to social media to complain about the seemingly late change set to be enforced.

One posted: “There will be England fans having to change flights if the Mexico game is moved.

“Pretty outrageous. Fans again treated like dirt.”

A second wrote: “Most fans will be happy. Only fans paying to go to a game will not.”

A fourth said: “Got to feel bad for the England fans with late flights booked.”



Another added: “I don’t know how serious the weather will be but no denying fans have been walloped (again).”

England are staying in Santa Fe ahead of the match at the daunting Azteca on Sunday.

Sports.title: Harry Kane reveals Eberechi Eze does NOT know words to Wonderwall after viral World Cup moment ‘we’ll remember forever’
Sports.content:
EBERECHI EZE doesn’t know the words to Wonderwall.

That is despite the England team and fans adopting the iconic Oasis song as their honorary World Cup anthem.





After every match, the players, led by Harry Kane, have formed a wall in front of the travelling England supporters and sung along to the Oasis tune playing over the speakers.

But after a comical moment at the end of the DR Congo game, which went viral on social media, Kane admitted on Lions Den that Eze doesn’t even know the words.

The England captain said: “I asked him, ‘Do you know the words?’ and he said no, so I need to teach him.

“In the last game, we didn’t celebrate enough or take in the moment of what we had achieved in finishing top of the group.



“No matter who we played against, we did an amazing job.

“I got the players together just to remind them to enjoy the moment and sing with the fans; they are here for us.

“Hearing Wonderwall and listening to 40,000 fans singing it back is something we will remember forever.

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“It’s hard to take it all in.”



Fans at home have certainly been relishing the 1995 hit in bars, in pubs, and at home.

Spotify streaming data shows that after the game, the tune experienced a listening spike of 210% in the UK.

Perhaps a few listens for Eze wouldn’t go amiss, so that he can sing along if England get past Mexico in the round of 16.

Hopefully, Kane delivers again and will have everyone singing from the same hymn sheet at full-time in the Azteca Stadium.

Sports.title: ‘Kick in stomach’ – Mexico boss SLAMS decision to change England World Cup kickoff time forcing him to change gameplan
Sports.content:
MEXICO boss Javier Aguirre has slammed the proposed decision to change the kickoff time of their World Cup clash against England.

The El Tri chief has been preparing to face the Three Lions on Sunday night at 6pm local time (1am UK, 8pm ET).





However, it is expected to be brought forward SIX HOURS to midday local time (7pm UK, 2pm ET).

Severe thunderstorms around the Azteca Stadium in Mexico City have seen the start time set to move, causing chaos.

And the Mexico manager has raged over the decision, forcing him to change his game plan.

He told radio station Grupo Formula: “Like a kick in the stomach because clearly you change everything, the game plan, everything.

“Not that everything goes down the drain, but almost because you’re changing six hours.

“I don’t like it at all, but evidently we will abide by what FIFA says.

“But I especially don’t like any of it, and neither do my players.”

He also confirmed that Fifa had informed him of the move on Friday afternoon.



He added it is: “Not a minor change. The change is important.

“I can understand their reasoning and arguments, but nobody consulted me. I’m very upset.”

England boss Thomas Tuchel‘s plans have also been thrown into chaos with the change.

However, fans at home will be delighted with the move.



It will now start on Sunday evening instead of the early hours of Monday morning.

Sports.title: World Cup LIVE: England vs Mexico kick-off change, Argentina vs Cape Verde suspension risk
Sports.content:
The World Cup is continuing to conjure up all sorts of news and headlines, with England preparing to face Mexico in their last-16 tie

England are currently preparing to face Mexico in their last-16 tie in the World Cup, and there have been reports that the kick-off time could be changed.

Spain eased into the last 16 of the World Cup by sweeping Austria aside 3-0. Mikel Oyarzabal scored a brace and Tottenham defender Pedro Porro also found the net to overcome Ralf Rangnick's side.

It was a classy and clinical display which will banish many people's memories of their 0-0 draw with Cape Verde in their first match. After Spain strode into the next round, a hint about Cristiano Ronaldo's next move was seemingly dropped by his sister Katia, before Portugal took on Croatia in the round of 32.

Meanwhile, the British government has confirmed pubs will be allowed to stay open for England's World Cup clash against Mexico. Thomas Tuchel's side face the co-hosts in Mexico City in the round of 16 next Monday, with the clash kicking off at 1am.

Pubs had already been given permission to stay open until 2am for England's knockout matches kicking off at 9pm and 10pm. However, under those original rules, they would not have been able to broadcast the entirety of the clash against the Mexicans while also remaining within the time period.

They will now be allowed to open after Sir Keir Starmer relaxed licensing rules. This update comes shortly after Tuchel urged families to either allow their children to stay up and watch the game, or even miss school in its entirety.

Portugal and Croatia had no shortage of drama as Cristiano Ronaldo finally got on the scoresheet in a knockout match. He equalised before Goncalo Ramos scored a stoppage-time winner and Croatia had a goal brutally ruled out for offside even later.

Then it's a 4am start for Switzerland against Algeria, with Swiss star Granit Xhaka the subject of transfer speculation back in the Premier League as Chelsea chase a deal for the Sunderland star.

Sports.title: Gary Neville hammers FIFA for "willy nilly" changing England game as integrity questioned
Sports.content:
Gary Neville hammers FIFA for "willy nilly" changing England game as integrity questioned

Former England defender Gary Neville was up in arms over the World Cup change some 48 hours before the Three Lions' encounter with Mexico

View Image Gary Neville has taken aim at FIFA following plans to change kick-off for England's clash with Mexico.

Gary Neville has criticised FIFA for their 'willy-nilly' change as he feels England are at a 'disadvantage' for their World Cup last-16 clash with Mexico. Three Lions bosses have been left stunned by the prospect of their showdown with the co-hosts as their encounter could be brought forward six hours due to the threat of adverse weather.

‌



England were due to take on Javier Aguirre's side at 1am (UK time) but the proposed move will see them kick-off at noon local time. The forecasted inclement weather means that there is a threat of thunderstorms and potential flooding in Mexico City. But England and Mexican officials are said to have found out about the change at the 11th-hour.

‌



Thomas Tuchel had planned accordingly for the sweltering and uncomfortable conditions in the Mexico capital. However, the possible change from FIFA, which has yet to be confirmed, has scuppered plans and their preparations with the schedule focused on gearing up for a 6pm kick-off, local time.

‌



Neville, who was apart of the England coaching staff at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, believes the Three Lions' opponents have the upper hand.

He said: "I would find it disruptive yeah, conditions are huge for England at a tournament we know that. We talk about heat a lot, playing at 12 in Mexico vs playing at six in the evening is very, very different.

So for the players, for our players, its worse, let's be really clear. Its a sporting disadvantage to England. There is a sporting integirty issue here as well because I've never seen a League Two game moved, I've never seen a Sunday League game moved. FIFA are sort of willy nilly making it up and moving a game.

‌



"It just feels a bit strange, you can put fan safety at the heart of it, but this stadium that has these conditions and would have a procedure to deal with that. To move a game two days out - I've never seen that at any level, ever."

The former Manchester United captain continued: “In 2014, I was part of the coaching staff that went to Brazil and we played our first game at altitude in Manaus.

“And you prepare every single minute of detail - obviously, we lost that game, but we played quite well in the first half - but you do prepare everything in relation to the conditions, kick-off time, when you fly in, so you’re exposed to the altitude at the right time.

‌



“It will be disruptive to England, they will not like this. The players, they’ll get on with it and they’ll never put anything negative out because they can’t because they would be defeatist. But if FIFA do do this, it is a disadvantage to England’s players and their preparations.”

While England may be left feeling aggrieved by being blind-sided by the decision from the tournament organisers, they aren't the only ones with Agiurre angered by the lack of consultation.

He said on Friday: "Like a kick in the stomach because clearly you change everything, the game plan, everything. Not that everything goes down the drain, but almost because you're changing six hours.

‌



"I don't like it at all, but evidently we will abide by what FIFA says. But I especially don't like any of it, and neither do my players.

"Not a minor change, the change is important," added the Mexico boss. "I can understand their reasoning and arguments, but nobody consulted me. I'm very upset."

Sports.title: Egypt down Australia in World Cup shootout as massive goalkeeper gamble backfires
Sports.content:
Egypt down Australia in World Cup shootout as massive goalkeeper gamble backfires

AUSTRALIA 0-0 (Pens: 3-4) EGYPT: After they couldn't be separated after 120 minutes the Egyptian secured victory on penalties to march into the last eight of the World Cup with a goalkeeper change in the final minute not paying off

Egypt are through to the quarter-finals of the World Cup after securing a 4-3 victory on penalties in Dallas.

‌



The Australians made the bold move of changing their goalkeeper with 120 minutes on the clock as ex-Arsenal shotstopper Mat Ryan coming on to replace Patrick Beach, who had been excellent during the game.

‌



The move would not pay off as Harry Souttar blazed over with the first penalty of the shootout and youngster Lucas Herrington hit the bar - meaning Egypt only needed four of their five penalties as they scored with every effort.

Mohamed Salah stepped up and slotted a panenka before Hossam Abdelmaguid sent Ryan the wrong way to seal victory for the Pharaohs.

Sports.title: Mexico boss confirms England World Cup kick off time change in furious FIFA rant
Sports.content:
Mexico boss confirms England World Cup kick off time change in furious FIFA rant

Mexico's head coach Javier Aguirre has seemingly confirmed that their last 16 clash with England has changed despite there still being no official word from FIFA

View 2 Images Mexico's head coach Javier Aguirre is unhappy with FIFA for changing their kick-off time against England

Mexico boss Javier Aguirre has confirmed England's World Cup last 16 clash has been switched to an earlier kick-off - and hit out at FIFA over the "kick in the gut."

‌



FIFA are still yet to officially confirm the game has been moved forward six hours due to electrical thunderstorms but Aguirre has seemingly been consulted on the matter and is infuriated by the disruption.

‌



He told Spanish-Mexican journalist Joaquin López Doriga on Radio Formula: “That’s right, it’s like a kick in the gut, it changes everything, the plan. It’s not that it’s completely ruined, but almost, because you have to swallow six hours of scheduled training.

‌



"Obviously, we will abide by what FIFA says. I don’t like it at all, nor do my players. Of course, the food, the nap, the sleep, the physiotherapy, everything, everything, it seems trivial, but it isn't.

England stunned as FIFA plan World Cup kick-off change as bosses express major concern READ MORE :

"Today, 60 people are working here so that these 26 friends can go out on Sunday and win the game, I mean, it's not a small thing, the truth is that the change is quite important and I'll tell you this, well, I can understand reasons and arguments, but they didn't consult me and yes, I'm quite angry."

The game was initially set for 6pm local time (1am UK) but has now seemingly been switched to 12pm local (7pm Sunday UK).

‌



When asked if the change gives the hosts an advantage at the Azteca Stadium, Aguirre responded emphatically: “Not at all, zero, name, no advantage whatsoever.

"In the contrary, I tell you this is all designed so, since that day in Ecuador we talked, we knew the schedule, we knew the venue, we didn't know the opponent, that's true, but in the end, yes, they screw me over a little, yes, well yes, we have no choice but to abide by what FIFA says."

View 2 Images England were left in the dark by FIFA, who had planned the changes behind their back (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

‌



England were left in the dark by FIFA and FA chiefs only found out there was a chance for a potential change when they noticed rumours swirling on social media amongst Mexican journalists.

Mirror Football also contacted the Mexican Football Federation, who also insisted at the time that they had not been consulted about any potential change.

A number of England fans are also due to arrive in Mexico City from Heathrow Airport on Sunday at 2pm local time, meaning they would miss the game.

‌



The FA is understood to be seriously concerned about the impact this change will have upon England fans who are travelling from far and wide to see their team in a historic fixture at one of football's great cathedrals.

Article continues below

There will be more to follow on this breaking news story and Mirror Sport will bring you the very latest updates, pictures and video as soon as possible. Please check back regularly for updates on this developing story.

Sports.title: England handed altitude lifeline after World Cup kick-off time vs Mexico 'brought forward'
Sports.content:
England handed altitude lifeline after World Cup kick-off time vs Mexico 'brought forward'

EXCLUSIVE: The England players could benefit from the six-hour kick off difference for their World Cup Round of 16 tie vs Mexico, as a shorter time spent at altitude provides a key benefit

View 7 Images England have seen their kick-off time changed for the clash with Mexico (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

England have been handed an altitude lifeline in their Round of 16 World Cup tie against Mexico, after the kick off time was set to be brought forward.

‌



The Three Lions faced a gruelling couple of days in Mexico City ahead of the match, faced with the prospect of altitude sickness and pandemonium outside their hotel. But, a slight change to the kick-off time could help to alleviate the challeging effects of being 7,200ft above sea level.

‌



FIFA reportedly told the FA earlier today that the kick-off time would change from 6pm local time on Sunday (1am on Monday in the UK) to 12pm (7pm UK time). The change came after Mexico City was forecast huge thunderstorms into Sunday evening, which threatened delaying kick-off into the early hours.

‌



View 7 Images Harry Kane got England out of jail against DR Congo (Image: Getty Images)

England's best chance of negating the effects of the Azteca stadium's altitude was to delay flying into the capital city until as late as possible, seeing as it wasn't possible to arrive a week in advance. The schedule change would now mean the oxygen reduction would have even less of an impact, it's been claimed.

Human performance expert Steve Magness told the Mirror: "Between 24 and 48 hours is where we your plasma volume hits the worst point. So think of your blood as free-flowing or essentially like sludge. Is the motorway open or is there a traffic jam?

‌



"The more blood plasma volume you have, the more it's likely to be free-flowing. As that gets reduced [with altitude], it becomes a little like a traffic jam, where it's like sludge and it takes longer to transport.

View 7 Images Mexico supporters pose outisde the Azteca stadium

"When we get to altitude, immediately our blood plasma volume starts going down because of the stress, and that like dips to the highest level after about two days."

‌



The England players could therefore benefit from the six-hour kick off difference, he added. Mr Magness, who wrote 'Win The Inside Game' and 'Do Hard Things', said the shorter time spent at altitude would provide a minor benefit, but it's still going to be tough for the Three Lions.

"At this point we're playing with the small details. I don't think [the kick-off time change] is doom or gloom. I don't think it's good or bad necessarily.

"It's six hours difference - it might make a minor difference for some players, but I think it's just kind of going to suck.

‌



"The reason for that is pretty simple; once you step off that plane, your body is freaking out. It almost overcorrects for the first two or three days. Um, but like it takes time to overcorrect. You benefit if you can get there before the stress peaks, which is about two to two-and-a-half days."

View 7 Images Thunderstorms were forecast at the Azteca stadium (Image: (Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

An intimidating atmosphere awaits at the Azteca, while the visitors are braced for hostility outside the team hotel. But altitude could be the biggest challenge, with the match taking place more than 2,000 metres above sea level.

‌



England manager Thomas Tuchel said: "My understanding is that we cannot adapt to the altitude. That is just a huge advantage that Mexico will have. It just takes too much time.

"We have only three days in between [the last-32 win over DR Congo and the Mexico game]. This is physically just not possible to adapt to the altitude, which is quite high.

View 7 Images England fans have flocked to Mexico City (Image: World Cup 2026 News Pool (WCNP))

‌



"We knew that before, so this is just something, it's just a disadvantage, with which we will have to deal. I think we showed the attitude that we are ready for that and from there we go."

Under safety rules, games face an automatic 30-minute delay if lightning strikes within eight miles of the stadium, with the clock resetting each time there is a new strike.

FIFA's World Cup regulations say the governing body has "the right to cancel, reschedule or relocate one or more matches... for any reason at its sole discretion, including as a result of force majeure or due to health, safety or security concerns".

‌



View 7 Images Fans were jubilant after England's 2-1 win against DR Congo (Image: Javier Garcia/Shutterstock)

England playmaker Morgan Rogers said of the potential change: "It's just another obstacle to overcome. We'll be ready regardless of the time.

"Earlier the better because you want to play. There is enough thinking about what is going to happen and the build-up - you just want to play the game.

‌



"Getting that adrenaline out there will help us and get us going and playing. We're looking forward to it whatever the time is.

"I'm not concerned about it, but won't be happy if it wakes me up, I'll be honest. We'll deal with it as best as possible. It's another obstacle to get over."

View 7 Images Thomas Tuchel hugging Harry Kane after the win over DR Congo (Image: ISI Photos via Getty Images)

‌



England team-mate Marcus Rashford also downplayed the impact of a potential kick-off change.

"I think for us it's the same, how we prepare for the game," the forward said. "It has to be the same, we have to be focused, we have to be ready for anything.

"I think it's one strength of the group, everyone included, the players, the staff, we're ready for whatever challenges get thrown at us. Obviously it's not ideal, but also it doesn't matter."

Article continues below

A kick-off alteration would only add to what England boss Tuchel knew would be "a lot, a lot, a lot of obstacles" awaiting them in Mexico.

Sports.title: Horror weather maps show why Mexico vs England kick-off time 'brought FORWARD' as huge thunderstorms hit Azteca
Sports.content:
Horror weather maps show why Mexico vs England kick-off time 'brought FORWARD' as huge thunderstorms hit Azteca

England's World Cup clash with Mexico was moved forward

View 4 Images Just days ago Starmer allowed pubs to stay open until 5am (Image: Getty Images)

England’s next World Cup clash has been brought forward, after thunderstorms were forecast to batter Mexico City.

‌



The match had been due to kick off at 1am UK time on Monday morning, but fans will now tune in hours earlier after FIFA reportedly made the rare decision to change the start time to 7pm UK time on Sunday night. Horror weather maps and forecasts suggested major thunderstorms and heavy rain were forecasts to batter Mexico City around the original kick-off.

‌



Forecasts showed almost 5mm of rain falling over the Banorte Stadium, which is more commonly known as the Azteca, with a huge band of stormy weather stretching across the Mexican capital. Under tournament safety rules, any lightning strike detected within an eight-mile radius of the stadium triggers an automatic 30-minute delay to play.

‌



View 4 Images This isn't the first time a game has been delayed (Image: Getty Images)

A similar threat caused disruption elsewhere at the tournament. France’s group-stage clash with Iraq was delayed by more than two hours after severe weather hit Philadelphia.

‌



FIFA's World Cup regulations also give organisers the power to “cancel, reschedule or relocate” fixtures “at its sole discretion”, allowing matches to be moved if safety concerns arise. Asked about the possibility of a schedule change before FIFA confirmed the decision, England winger Marcus Rashford admitted it was “not ideal” but insisted the squad would be ready.

View 4 Images Mexico is facing thunderous weather throughout Sunday night

He said: "I think for us it’s the same how we prepare for the game - it has to be the same. We have to be focused. We have to be ready for anything. I think it’s one of our strengths as a group.

‌



“Everyone, including the players and staff… we are ready for whatever challenges get thrown at us. So obviously it’s not ideal but also it doesn’t really matter.”

View 4 Images Fifa’s World Cup regulations give organisers the power to “cancel, reschedule or relocate” fixtures

The late switch came just days after Keir Starmer confirmed pubs across England and Wales would be allowed to stay open until 5am if needed so supporters could watch England’s overnight World Cup fixtures.

Article continues below

The Prime Minister relaxed alcohol licensing laws, meaning pubs and bars no longer needed to apply for special late licences. England’s clash in Mexico City had originally been expected to finish after 3am UK time, with the possibility of running even later if it went to penalties.

Sports.title: England camp break silence as Mexico kick-off time to be changed for World Cup clash
Sports.content:
England camp break silence as Mexico kick-off time to be changed for World Cup clash

England have been left stunned by FIFA's decision to bring their Round of 16 clash with Mexico forward

View 2 Images (Image: PA Wire)

England star Marcus Rashford has described the Round of 16 kickoff change against Mexico as 'not ideal', while team-mate Morgan Rogers insists the sudden alteration is merely another obstacle for the Three Lions to overcome.

‌



Football Association (FA) bosses have been left in the dark over FIFA's decision to bring the clash with Mexico forward to 7pm amid the risk of flooding, thunderstorms and adverse weather conditions at the Azteca Stadium in Mexico City.

‌



England had been due to lock horns with the co-hosts at 1am GMT, but reports emerged on Friday evening that tournament organisers had concocted plans to bring the kick-off forward several hours. Mirror Football understands that The FA only found out about these plans via the media.

‌



England stunned as FIFA plan World Cup kick-off change as bosses express major concern READ MORE :

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

Rashford said: "I think for us it's the same how we prepare for the game. We have to be focused. We have to be ready for anything. I think it's one of our strengths as a group.

"Everyone, including the players and staff... we are ready for whatever challenges get thrown at us. So obviously it's not ideal but also it doesn't really matter."

‌



Aston Villa playmaker Rogers has been a impact substitute off the bench for Thomas Tuchel's side in the opening four matches. He has been forced to play deputy to Real Madrid powerhouse Jude Bellingham. England's preparations for the clash with Mexico have been overshadowed by the altitude that faces the Three Lions with the Azteca 2,200 metres above sea-level.

View 2 Images Julian Quinones has been one of the starring figures for Mexico and will be looking to down England. (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

The co-hosts are also threatening to make it a hostile welcome for the 1966 World Cup winners. Mexico have already been the subject of a complaint from Ecuador for their gamesmanship on the eve of their Round of 32 encounter when supporters took the streets overnight to disrupt their preparations but Rogers sees it as "just another obstacle to overcome".

‌



He said: "We'll take it how it is. Whatever it is, whatever the task is in front of us, whatever problem we face, or different things that might be a bit difficult, we're just going to attack it full front and be ready as a whole team and be together and talk through what can help us, what can be difficult, and just try and overcome it."

The protocols surrounding electrical storms are based upon recommendations from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), as opposed to tournament organisers FIFA. According to their guidelines, matches must be halted and suspended if there is a discharge detected within an eight-mile radius of the stadium.

Players and staff will then be forced to exit the pitch while supporters are advised to find shelter at the stadium. With the Azteca design not possessing a retractable roof, spectators could be at risk. For the game to restart, there must be no further lightning strikes detected within that eight-mile radius of the venue for a full 30 minutes.

Article continues below

After 30 minutes, if there is no further disruption, fans can return to their seats, and players will return to the pitch for a 15-minute warm-up before the game restarts. The decision to change England's kick-off time is also said to have a knock-on effect on the other Round of 16 encounter between Brazil and Norway.

Erling Haaland and Gabriel's bitter reunion could be moved back an hour due to extreme heat in New York. The National Weather Service has forecast disruption during the Fourth of July weekend celebrations with Philadelphia and Washington DC expected to reach 104F (40C) and 103F, respectively.

Sports.title: Egypt eliminate Australia from World Cup after penalty shoot-out drama
Sports.content:
Egypt are into the last 16 of the World Cup after beating Australia in a dramatic penalty shoot-out in Dallas.

The game itself ended 1-1 after extra time but Harry Souttar and Lucas Herrington both missed from the spot in the shootout while Egypt converted four consecutive spot-kicks against Mat Ryan - brought on in the 119th minute - to send Australia packing.

Although Cristian Volpato's early effort skimmed the crossbar, it was Egypt who were the better team in the first half and Emam Ashour soon nodded them in front. Omar Marmoush should have doubled the advantage at the start of the second period.

Image: Emam Ashour heads Egypt in front against Australia at the World Cup

But Egypt were punished when Australia found an equaliser that came when Mohamed Hany glanced the ball into his own net. It still took a stunning save from Patrick Beach to deny Ramy Rabia a 94th-minute winner and take the game to extra time.

Mohamed Salah came to life in extra-time but could not force the winner and Egypt would have been entitled to feel concerned by the prospect of penalties having lost their previous four shoot-outs - particularly when Ryan came on in goal for Australia.

The experienced stopper replaced Beach but could not keep out any Egypt penalties, Salah dinking his effort down the middle. Two Australia defenders missed - Souttar and Herrington - to end their hopes as Egypt set up a clash with Argentina or Cape Verde.

Image: Egypt's Mohamed Salah comforts Australia's Aziz Behich after Australia's loss

5 - CROSSBAR! Volpato took a shot from distance that skimmed the bar.

13 - GOAL! Ashour nodded Egypt ahead when unmarked at the back.

21 - WIDE! Zico fired wide when through but was adjudged offside.

46 - WIDE! Marmoush straight from the restart slotted his shot wide.

55 - OWN GOAL! Australia levelled when the ball glances in off Hany.

90+4 - SAVE! Beach brilliantly pushed Rabia's header over the bar.

PEN - MISS! Souttar blazed the opening penalty over the crossbar.

PEN - MISS! After five conversions, Herrington hit the bar himself.

PEN - WINNER! Abdelmaguid sent Ryan the wrong way to win it.

Salah: If anyone was going to Panenka, it was going to be me!

Egypt captain Mohamed Salah speaking on BBC Sport: "It's history. I told the boys before the game 'this is the biggest stage you can play in your life so just enjoy it. Don't let the pressure get to you and not enjoy the moment.'

"I'm glad we managed to win the game. Bad luck for them [Australia]...

On his Panenka penalty: "If someone was going to do it, it was going to be me.

"I'm more experienced than others, I want to give them confidence but I decided last minute [on the run-up]. I don't know if it's my last World Cup or not, so I had to do it."

On possibly facing Messi in the round of 16: "We have to respect both teams and we'll see what's next."

Sports.title: Sabalenka sets up mouth-watering Wimbledon clash with Osaka
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka set up a mouth-watering Wimbledon clash with Naomi Osaka as Coco Gauff matched her best run, while Novak Djokovic and Jannik Sinner continue their title pursuit.

Sabalenka came through a power-packed battle with Jelena Ostapenko to set up a fourth-round showdown with Osaka.

Sabalenka and Osaka first met at the US Open in 2018, with the Japanese star going on to win her maiden Grand Slam title, but had not faced each other again until Indian Wells this spring.

Remarkably, this will be their fourth meeting in as many months, all in the last 16, with Sabalenka also beating Osaka in Madrid and at the French Open.

Until this season, grass would have been seen as the least likely surface for Osaka to cause an upset, but the former world No 1 has been in fine form this month.

Osaka reached her first final on grass in Germany ahead of Wimbledon and is yet to drop a set at the All England Club, with her 6-1 6-3 victory over Daria Kasatkina putting her through to the fourth round here for the first time.

The 28-year-old walked out on Court One wearing another version of her Japanese-inspired outfit, this time featuring a floor-length robe with flowing draped sleeves.

While her recent record against Sabalenka has not been good, Osaka is not unhappy about facing the top seed again.

"I have only lost to her and Iga [Swiatek] for the past couple of months," she said. "Hey, a win is a win. I'll take that.

"Also, she's the number one player in the world. If there is someone I had to lose to, I would pick that ranking position. I would say I learned from all of those matches, so hopefully I can apply [it]."

Image: Sabalenka celebrates her victory against Jelena Ostapenko

Sabalenka's clash with former French Open champion Ostapenko was always going to be a first-strike battle between two of the hardest hitters on tour.

Ostapenko has a strong track record on grass having made the semi-finals here back in 2018 and won two titles on the surface - two more than Sabalenka - but the world No 1 was just a little bit better in a 6-4 6-4 success.

On playing Osaka, Sabalenka said: "Another aggressive player, a very powerful match. I'm ready to bring the fire, to fight and to do anything it takes to get through."

The two-time Grand Slam winner has struggled to master the surfaces of the All England Club since famously stunning five-time champion Venus Williams on her debut at the age of 15.

Against a compatriot ranked 139 places below her, Gauff breezed through the opening set but squandered three match points at 5-4 up before losing the second set tie-break with a double fault.

The world No 7 eventually prevailed 6-3 6-7 (5-7) 6-2 in two hours and 26 minutes to match her best run at the Championships.

Djokovic suffered a shock exit in the last 32 of the French Open last month and while he prevented a repeat at the All England Club on Friday afternoon, a 7-5 6-4 1-6 7-6 (7-4) victory only told half the story for the 24-time Grand Slam singles winner.

Frenchman Rinderknech had been two points away from dishing out the 13th 6-0 score of Djokovic's career during an extraordinary 18-minute third set on Centre Court, but the 39-year-old avoided that unwanted feat and regrouped in set four to go through.

The defending champion suffered a fall and a bloodied foot in a five-set battle with Miomir Kecmanovic in round one, followed by a two-and-a-half-hour, two tie-break tussle with Nuno Borges two days ago.

So a relatively straightforward 6-4 6-3 6-4 win, in two hours and 14 minutes, was most welcome for the Italian.

"I'm very happy about the win," he said. "I'm trying to improve every day, it's a small step forward today. I'm trying to get better if I want to go far in this tournament."

There was the odd sticky moment, however, despite American Brooksby arriving in London this summer on a nine-match losing streak.

Sports.title: Wilder would welcome Usyk fight, says co-manager
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder's co-manager Shelly Finkel has confirmed that the American former world heavyweight champion would welcome a fight against Oleksandr Usyk.

Usyk is reportedly targeting a fight with Wilder after vacating his WBC, IBF and WBA belts to free him from his mandatory title commitments.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oleksandr Usyk announces on his Instagram that he is to vacate all world titles but teases 'last dance'.

Finkel told Sky Sports: "If the terms were right, Deontay would welcome the opportunity to fight Usyk.

"Usyk is a great champion and it would be an honour to fight him."

Previously Wilder told Sky Sports why he wanted to fight Usyk: "He's one of the best in the era. I do need him to accomplish what I need to accomplish.

"It can happen and it will happen. As long as I have the confidence to do what I have to do, it will happen.

"I must accomplish what I set forth in the beginning of my career."

Usyk's final world title fight was against kickboxing star Rico Verhoeven. Although Usyk's late stoppage victory has prompted much debate a potential rematch with Verhoeven is considered unlikely.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oleksandr Usyk survived an incredible performance from kickboxing legend Rico Verhoeven as the fight was waved off with seconds remaining in the eleventh round. Highlights courtesy of DAZN and Ring Magazine.

His team also all but ruled out a trilogy fight with Tyson Fury before the end of his career.

Sergey Lapin, the CEO of Usyk's promotional company Ready To Fight, told Sky Sports: "I don't really see much point in it. Oleksandr has already beaten Tyson Fury twice and answered every question inside the ring.

Usyk-Wilder would most likely be held in America, though Usyk does still harbour a dream of boxing one last time in his Ukrainian homeland. That has been impossible for the former Olympic and undisputed champion since Russia launched its full scale invasion of Ukraine.

"Saudi Arabia and the United States are both outstanding venues for major events. But if we're talking about a dream, it would undoubtedly be Ukraine," Lapin said.

Sports.title: YouTuber Brad Dalke in contention for title on DP World Tour debut
Sports.content:
YouTube golfer Brad Dalke finds himself challenging for the title on his DP World Tour debut at the BMW International Open, sitting two shots off the lead at the halfway stage in Munich after a second-round 66.

Best known for his contributions to the popular Good Good YouTube golf channel, Dalke is playing the tournament on a sponsor's exemption and catapulted himself into contention with a six-under 66 on Friday that contained seven birdies and one dropped shot on the par-four 15th.

His score was bettered only by England's Jack Senior's 65 which has him in a share of second on 10 under, one behind leader Hennie du Plessis of South Africa, who followed up his opening 64 with a 69 on day two.

Countryman Michael Hollick and Mexico's Carlos Ortiz are tied with Senior in second, while American Dalke has further English hopefuls Paul Wearing and Joe Dean and Frederic Lacroix for company at nine under.

The 28-year-old Dalke was somewhat of a golfing prodigy in his youth, winning the 2015 Junior PGA Championship and finishing as runner-up at the US Amateur a year later which earned him a spot at both The Masters and US Open in 2017, where he failed to make the cut at either.

Making his first appearance in a ranking event for six years, Dalke said: "I didn't really have a goal coming into this week. I just wanted to have some fun and enjoy it, and obviously shooting 66 is pretty fun, so that helps the cause.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brad Dalke left himself in contention going into the third round, of his first DP World Tour event, after a fantastic second round

"Yesterday, that first tee shot, I was shaking like a leaf, and then coming down the last few holes too.

"I try not to look at leaderboards, but it's hard not to miss them out there, seeing my name up there for the first time.

"It's very nervy, but I also love these moments. I love playing in front of big crowds and big opportunities. It's been fun."

He added: "It's a weird mixture of there's no stress because I'm not out here fighting for points and I'm not grinding every week on the [DP World Tour] season, but also I do kind of represent YouTube golf in a way.

"There's a lot of people who love YouTube and love watching me, and they vouch for me, so I'm trying to prove it for them as well."

Sports.title: Hamilton storms to Silverstone Sprint pole in flying start at British GP
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has made a storming start to the British Grand Prix weekend by claiming pole position for Saturday's Sprint at Silverstone.

On a weekend he will go in search of a landmark 10th victory at his home race in Sunday's main Grand Prix, Hamilton made the perfect start on Friday by topping practice and then all three segments of Sprint Qualifying to pip Mercedes' title-leading Kimi Antonelli to pole by 0.011s.

It marks the seven-time world champion's first pole position in either of Formula 1's qualifying formats since last season's Sprint in China, which he won, and maintains the 41-year-old's growing momentum in his second year at Ferrari three weeks after winning the race in Barcelona.

Hamilton had strongly played down Ferrari's prospects at Silverstone in interviews on Thursday owing to Ferrari's supposed straight-line speed deficit to championship leaders Mercedes.

But on a high-speed circuit where power is king, the Ferrari SF-26 looked competitive from the outset, with Hamilton producing another masterclass around Silverstone to lead the resurgent Scuderia's charge again.

A jubilant Hamilton, whose pole was cheered by the large Friday crowd at a sun-kissed circuit, said afterwards that Ferrari's form relative to Mercedes so far had come as an "amazing surprise".

Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle said: "Lewis made the difference. That was a classic Lewis Hamilton Silverstone lap."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reflects on claiming pole for the British Grand Prix Sprint race

With Antonelli just falling short of Hamilton in second, Max Verstappen took third in the improved Red Bull to complete an eye-catching one-two-three on the grid for Saturday's 17-lap Sprint.

But Charles Leclerc could again not match Hamilton in the sister Ferrari, lapping three tenths slower than his team-mate to take fourth. But Leclerc was still ahead of Austria victor George Russell, who struggled relative to Antonelli throughout the session and could only manage fifth place in an early blow to his own home race weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton claims Sprint Pole at the British Grand Prix!

World champions McLaren were never a factor in the pole fight.

Lando Norris, who carried car damage through the first two segments before repairs ahead of SQ3, eventually pipped team-mate Oscar Piastri to sixth but the McLaren duo, whose cars are running in throwback white and green livery this weekend, wound up four tenths off the pace.

2) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) George Russell, Mercedes



6) Lando Norris, McLaren



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



9) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



10) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls

Isack Hadjar had run ahead of Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen in SQ1 but eventually slipped to eighth on the soft tyres, although still lapped only a tenth behind the third-placed Dutchman.

Hadjar stayed ahead of the Racing Bulls pair of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, who continued their consistent top-10 form of recent weeks.

'We really, really didn't' - Hamilton stunned to outpace Mercedes

Given he had talked down Ferrari's prospects of beating Mercedes this weekend, Hamilton admitted he was surprised to be ahead in the weekend's first battle for pole.

"We're ahead of a Mercedes and the Red Bull, they have so much power these guys," he said.

"They've been doing amazing all year, the boys in blue (Mercedes) this weekend, these champs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Ant Davidson shows how Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was able to edge out Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli for Sprint pole at the British GP

"But my team won't let up, they'll keep pushing, and that's what I'm so proud of.

"It won't always be like this, but we didn't expect coming to Silverstone that we'd be competing for the front row, we really, really didn't."

Antonelli, who leads Russell by 40 points and Hamilton by 46 points in the Drivers' Championship, had looked the more comfortable of the two Mercedes drivers on Friday but fell narrowly short of ensuring a Silver Arrow pole.

"The car felt good," said the Italian teenager.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes drivers Kimi Antonelli and George Russell reflect on their performance during the Sprint Qualifying session at the British Grand Prix

"Ferrari have done an incredible step forward, so definitely it's going to be very tough. Plus, Lewis is in great form, but that's good, we like the challenge and we'll try to make the best out of it.

"Of course (I can fight for the win tomorrow), we'll go for it and we'll try to do our best. It's not going to be easy, but everything is on the table to do well."

Sports.title: Hamilton eyes Silverstone Sprint win after 'amazing surprise' pole
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton said his British Grand Prix Sprint pole came as an "amazing surprise" but now believes his Ferrari is quick enough to claim victory at Silverstone in Saturday's shortened race.

The seven-time world champion had been highly pessimistic about his chances at his home race on Thursday, but answered his doubters by topping practice before edging Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli to pole by just 0.011 seconds.

Hamilton claimed his first Grand Prix victory for Ferrari in Barcelona last month, but it was followed by a disappointing weekend in Austria, where the Italian team's upgraded engine - introduced after concerns it lacked the power of Mercedes' and Red Bull's - struggled in the hot conditions.

Hamilton said: "We're ahead of a Mercedes and the Red Bull, they have so much power these guys."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reflects on claiming pole for the British Grand Prix Sprint race.

"They've been doing amazing all year, the boys in blue [Mercedes] this weekend, these champs, but my team won't let up, they'll keep pushing, and that's what I'm so proud of.

"It won't always be like this, but we didn't expect coming to Silverstone that we'd be competing for the front row, we really, really didn't, so, this is an amazing surprise. I'm ecstatic."

After pulling off the upset in a session where he and Antonelli appeared to be in a league of their own, Hamilton expressed belief that he might be able to keep the Italian, and Red Bull's Max Verstappen in third, behind him during the 17-lap contest.

Due to there being only one practice session on Sprint weekends, drivers have limited opportunity to simulate longer race runs, but Hamilton was pleased with his experience.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Ant Davidson shows how Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was able to edge out Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli for Sprint pole at the British GP.

"I think our pace was good," he added. "We did a short sort of longish run in practice. There wasn't a lot of time.

"But the car felt good there, so I think we should have a good race tomorrow.

"I mean, starting from the front row, I don't remember the last time I started from the front row here.

"Not so easy when you've got these guys that can follow you and be close with the extra power potentially, but I'll do my best to keep them behind."

Antonelli: Lewis is in form, but we like the challenge!

Antonelli, who leads the Drivers' Championship by 40 points from his team-mate George Russell, was on provisional pole before being edged out by Hamilton.

"It was so, so close, and it was a shame," Antonelli said.

"SQ1 I felt a bit bad, I didn't feel great in the car, but then we made a slight balance adjustment and SQ2 felt night and day, and we suddenly were back on the pace.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes drivers Kimi Antonelli and George Russell reflect on their performance during the Sprint Qualifying session at the British Grand Prix.

"SQ3 there was a little bit left on the table, but it was a decent lap, and unfortunately super close to Lewis.

"But congrats to him, and on our side, we'll focus on tomorrow now."

Hamilton is third in the standings, 46 points back from Antonelli, and the Italian is welcoming the challenge of the driver he replaced at Mercedes at the start of 2025.

He added: "Ferrari have done an incredible step forward, so definitely it's going to be very tough. Plus, Lewis is in great form, but that's good, we like the challenge and we'll try to make the best out of it.

"Of course [I can fight for the win tomorrow], we'll go for it and we'll try to do our best. It's not going to be easy, but everything is on the table to do well."

Verstappen: Hamilton and Antonelli look a bit quick

Verstappen came out on top of an extremely close battle for third, which saw four drivers - Charles Leclerc, George Russell, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri - finish within a tenth of a second of him.

The Dutchman was 0.321s behind Hamilton's leading effort, but just 0.075 clear of McLaren's Piastri in seventh.

For that reason, he was able to view the session positively but was also not overly optimistic about his chances of challenging the top two on Saturday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Red Bull's Max Verstappen responds to rumours linking him with McLaren.

Verstappen said: "It was very close, I could easily have been P3 or P6 or P7, but we were on the good side.

"We were a bit closer but we're still not where we want to be. Cornering, maybe a tiny bit, but also deployment stuff, so a few things to figure out to try to find more lap time. We'll try to do that of course after the Sprint.

"They [Hamilton and Antonelli] look a bit quick. And if they look quick, normally their team-mates should also be quick in race pace when everything calms down a little bit.

"So, for me, I think it will be more of a battle with the guys behind me."
